observations: A broad dark-brown rounded shape fills the canvas against a black ground, with two asymmetric ring-eyes built from concentric black and yellow circles with teal cross-hair centers, set at different heights.
A wide rectangular mouth sits in the lower third, outlined in white and black, filled with a row of blocky white teeth marked by short vertical black lines, with orange visible beneath.

Dense overlapping lines in magenta, yellow, blue, green, and white pack the interior of the face shape, while a tight zigzag wave runs along the top edge and a small artist signature appears at lower right.
reading: Two mismatched ring-eyes stare outward from a squat brown mass, one higher and larger than the other, giving the face an off-balance weight. The white-boxed teeth below read as a fixed, wide-open display rather than a smile. Layers of colored lines fill every gap, making the face feel dense and pressurized. The overall mood reads as confrontational, though that is a reading, not a fact.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #35 and #37. Where #35 uses a bright yellow outer frame and open line work on a busy ground, #36 pulls the face into a darker enclosed brown mass with color pushed inward.

connections.reason: Both works share concentric-ring eye forms and a wide toothed mouth zone, but #35 spreads its structure across a bright yellow border while #36 compresses the same elements into a dark enclosed shape.

Title neighbor #37 also uses a dark outer mass with ring eyes and visible teeth, but its eyes differ—one oval, one rectangular—offering a direct contrast in eye-form handling across adjacent works in the owned subset.

lookingQuestion: How does the difference in size and height between the two ring-eyes affect the way you read the balance of the face?
ambiguities: The zigzag line at the top edge could be read as a decorative border or as part of the face structure; the image does not resolve this.
The nnotb #206 comparison shows a spiral eye and toothed mouth but the overall composition and color field differ enough that no strong formal connection was found; it is omitted.
